title: Tanzanian Sugarcane Juice
community: Zanzibar and coastal Tanzania — the street vendor drink
author: Chef Fatuma
desc: Tanzanian Sugarcane Juice — freshly pressed sugarcane juice with a squeeze of lime and a pinch of ginger. The most refreshing drink in Tanzania — the sugarcane juice pressed on demand by hand or machine at every Zanzibar market corner.
longDesc: Sugarcane juice is the universal Tanzanian street drink — present at every market, every bus station, every beach. In Zanzibar, the pressed juice is sometimes served with ginger and lime, making it one of the most refreshing drinks in East Africa.
ingredients: 6—8 sticks fresh sugarcane — peeled and cut
equipment: Sugarcane press or heavy knife and blender
steps: If using a press: feed cane through the press. Collect juice.
If using a blender: chop cane finely, blend with a little water, strain through a cloth.
chefTips: Sugarcane juice oxidises quickly — drink within 30 minutes.
Lime and ginger are the Zanzibari additions.
commonMistakes: Not drinking quickly — juice turns sour.
cookingScience: Fresh sugarcane juice is particularly susceptible to oxidation — the polyphenol oxidase enzyme in the juice rapidly oxidises phenolic compounds when exposed to air. The citric acid from lime partially inhibits this enzyme, extending the juice's freshness.
sustainabilityTips: Sugarcane is widely grown in Tanzania — locally sourced.
culturalNote: Sugarcane juice from a Zanzibar market press — watched over ice with lime and ginger on a hot afternoon — is one of the island's greatest simple pleasures. It is the drink that makes the afternoon bearable.
